summary: Macro backdrop for ags: headwind (score -6 across rates, dollar, Brazil real, risk, energy, China, breadth). rates 0; dollar −; brl −; risk −; energy −; china −; breadth −. Strongest ag/soft over the month: Rough rice +3.7%; weakest: Lean hogs -15.8%. Key releases ahead: US FOMC Meeting Minutes (11-18 2:00 PM ET).

sections.title: Rates
sections.text: US 10-year 5.10% (+1 bp in a month), 2-year 4.80% (+6 bp); 2s10s curve +30 bp (-5 bp in a month). Yields are little changed on the month. T-bill yield 4.15% sets the cost of carrying inventory.

sections.title: Dollar & farm currencies
sections.text: Dollar index 103.79 (+1.8% in a month, +5.6% YTD). A stronger dollar makes US grain, oilseeds, cotton and meat dearer abroad. USD/BRL 5.796 (+14.5% in a month): a weaker real encourages Brazilian farmer selling of soybeans, corn, sugar, coffee and cotton, pressuring world prices. USD/CNY 6.668 (-0.3%); USD/MXN 18.55 (+0.6%).

sections.title: Risk appetite
sections.text: S&P 500 -4.2% in a month (+7.2% YTD); VIX 23.8. Risk-off: funds tend to cut commodity length along with equities.

sections.title: Energy
sections.text: WTI 85.04 $/bbl (-13.7% in a month), Brent 89.86, ULSD 4.040 $/gal (-14.5%), natural gas 3.26 (-2.7%). Lower crude weighs on soybean oil and corn through biofuel margins and on cotton via cheaper polyester.

sections.title: China & industrial demand
sections.text: Copper -12.9% in a month, Shanghai Composite -3.8%, Hang Seng -3.7%, yuan +0.3% vs USD. Soft China/industrial signals point to weaker import demand.

sections.title: Commodity breadth
sections.text: 7 of 33 commodities trade above their 50-day average (21%); S&P GSCI -10.5% in a month; gold -9.0%.

caveat: Directional channels from macro to ag prices are standard relationships, not signals tested on this desk; use as context.
